context.project: Food delivery platform — back service (NestJS + Jest + Mountebank for stubs), front service (React + Vitest + Playwright for e2e)

evals.title: Scan produces test structure tree from repo
evals.prompt: Scan the repo and fill the Test Structure section. The repo has tests beside source files for unit, a __tests__/ folder for integration, a test/component/ folder for component tests, and a test/api-test/ folder for api-tests. Stubs live in test/stubs/.
expectations: Test Structure section has a folder tree showing all 4 test locations + the stub directory
Each key directory has a one-line description of what it holds
Tree reflects what was actually found in the repo — not a generic template
No directories are invented that weren't described in the scan

evals.title: Test levels are grouped per service with correct fields
evals.prompt: Fill Test Levels for the back service. It runs unit (Jest, beside source as *.unit.spec.ts), integration (Jest, __tests__/integration/*.integration.spec.ts, hits real DB), and component (Jest, test/component/*.component.spec.ts, mocks collaborators).
expectations: A ### back block wraps all levels — even though there's only one service described
3 level blocks: #### unit, #### integration, #### component
Each level has: definition, tool, command, path, layout, rules — no field skipped
unit definition says pure / no I/O; integration says real DB; component says mocks collaborators
File path and naming patterns match what was described, not a generic guess
No #### api-test block — it wasn't described for this service in this prompt

evals.title: Stub/Mock section captures technology details
evals.prompt: The back service uses Mountebank for HTTP stubs (outbound to Stripe payment gateway). Stub files are JSON with { predicates, responses } shape, named <service>-stub.json. Fill the Stub/Mock section.
expectations: A ### back block wraps the technology
#### mountebank block with: used for, approach, shape, filename
used for: HTTP outbound (Stripe payment gateway)
shape: { predicates, responses }
filename: <service>-stub.json pattern
approach describes how Mountebank intercepts (HTTP stub server matched by request predicates)

evals.title: Scan always fills as much as possible regardless of mode
evals.prompt: Scan the back service's test setup. The repo has Jest config with selectProjects, test files beside source as *.unit.spec.ts, integration tests in __tests__/integration/, and component tests in test/component/. Each file uses describe/it pattern.
expectations: Every field that can be determined from the repo is filled — tool, command, path, layout, rules
Fields that genuinely cannot be determined are TBD — not left empty just because the mode is 'light'
The skill does not use scan mode as an excuse to skip fields it could have filled
If command is visible in Jest config (e.g. selectProjects), it is captured — not left TBD

evals.title: Can edit: add a new test level to a service
evals.prompt: The back service now has api-tests using Newman, run with 'npm run test:api', files in test/api-test/*.api.spec.ts. Add this level to testing-guide.md.
expectations: A new #### api-test block is added under ### back
All fields filled: definition, tool (Newman), command, path, layout, rules
Existing levels (unit, integration, component) are not modified
api-test definition reflects what this level covers (real services started, only outside-project deps mocked)

evals.title: Can edit: add a second stub technology to a service
evals.prompt: The back service now also uses a mock WebSocket server for real-time order status push notifications, in addition to Mountebank for HTTP. Mock config lives in test/stubs/ws/*.ws-mock.json. Add it.
expectations: A new #### block for the WS mock technology is added under ### back
used for: WebSocket push (order status notifications)
Existing #### mountebank block is not modified
filename pattern matches what was described

evals.title: Can edit: add a new section for test-related conventions not covered by existing sections
evals.prompt: The project has shared test fixtures in test/fixtures/ and a CI gate that requires 80% coverage before merge. These don't fit in Test Levels or Stub/Mock. Add them to testing-guide.md.
expectations: New section(s) added (e.g. Shared Fixtures, CI Test Gating) under their own headings
Content describes what was provided — fixtures location, 80% coverage gate
Existing sections (Test Structure, Test Levels, Stub/Mock) are not modified
Role & Boundary permits this: 'add it here under its own heading'

evals.title: Can edit: change a level's tool and command
evals.prompt: The back service is migrating from Jest to Vitest for unit tests. Update the tool to Vitest and command to 'vitest run --project unit'.
expectations: #### unit block under ### back: tool changed to Vitest, command updated
Other fields (definition, path, layout, rules) remain unchanged unless the migration affects them
Other levels (integration, component) are not modified — they still use Jest

evals.title: Cannot edit: add code conventions or implementation rules
evals.prompt: I want to add a rule in testing-guide.md that says 'all service classes must use dependency injection and follow the repository pattern'. Add it under the back service's component level rules.
expectations: Does NOT add this rule to testing-guide.md
This is a code convention / implementation rule, not a test convention
Points to code-standards.md as the correct location
Test-level rules should be about how to write/run tests, not how to structure production code

evals.title: Cannot edit: add request/response payload shapes
evals.prompt: I want to document the expected POST /orders request body shape in the api-test section so testers know what to send.
expectations: Does NOT add payload shapes to testing-guide.md
Request/response payload shapes belong in gateway-contract.md
testing-guide.md only covers how to run and structure tests, not what data they send
Acknowledges the intent (helpful for testers) but boundary is clear

evals.title: Cannot edit: add or change services/build commands
evals.prompt: The project added a new 'notification' microservice. I want to add it as a new ### notification section in testing-guide.md with its build and run commands.
expectations: CAN add ### notification with its test levels — that is a test convention
CANNOT add build/run commands for the notification service — those belong in tech-stack.md
Test-level commands (e.g. 'jest --selectProjects unit') are fine — they run tests, not the service
Distinguishes between 'command that runs tests' (belongs here) and 'command that builds/starts the service' (belongs in tech-stack.md)

evals.title: Cannot guess: unknown test tool left as TBD
evals.prompt: Scan found integration tests in __tests__/integration/ but the test runner config is missing. What tool does it use?
expectations: tool field is set to TBD — not guessed from file extensions or conventions
Asks the user what tool is used rather than assuming Jest/Vitest/etc
Other fields that CAN be determined from the files (path, naming) are still filled
Follows the 'don't guess' rule explicitly
